items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: I see what, uh, there was a guy called Shaw. ... He would take bands and, uh, bring them up as far as Lake Shaw. He would book them.

ctx.x: Um, he, alright, now, you just mentioned something else which I wanted to ask you about, is, this business about, um, going up north, leaving the city, going to Chicago and that thing. Did you ever think of that or did you ever feel like doing that? No, I never did.

I never felt that, I felt like I wanted to go to Chicago and to visit, you know, off here, which I've promised, uh, my wife died, I would think of. Uh, but, the city playing because I feel that I didn't read any reason, I knew I had to read, you know. Uh, I didn't, I wasn't making any money, uh, on the read. And I would do work behind here, playing a little, you know, and working. I felt I would move basically pure. And, and, and the only thing I would be if I'd have run away. And I never won, so. I would go on…

What, do you think that there would be something about the personalities or something of, of people that did want to leave? I mean, do you think that there was anything particular, I mean, would there be any particular kind of person that would be the kind of person that would want to leave, or, um, um, something about, uh, his style or anything like that? No, I don't think so.
